key_insight: Small, interpretable gene programs can predict which lupus nephritis patients will respond to specific therapies, but the signal varies strongly by treatment.
clinical_relevance: This could support enrichment-style trial design by identifying likely responders before treatment enrollment, especially for regimens with clear transcriptional signatures.
method: Reconstructed a lupus nephritis gene-expression cohort (GSE224705) with 21,914 genes across 319 samples.
Built treatment-specific responder vs non-responder models for MMF, AZA, hydroxychloroquine, and standard of care.
Used compact multi-gene programs and pathway enrichment to test predictive performance and biological stability.
evidence_signal: Five-to-ten gene programs achieved AUROC 0.847 for MMF and 0.866 for AZA, versus 0.718 for HC and 0.623 for SOC, with SOC near chance (MCC 0.119, balanced accuracy 0.555).
watch_item: These are retrospective, dataset-specific findings, so external validation and prospective testing are still needed before any real-world use.
paper_title: Interpretable biomarker programs predict treatment response in lupus nephritis: patient-level validation across four regimens
